title: On Information Propagation in Krylov Subspaces
authors: Pablo Martinez-Azcona, Maximilian Meyer-Moelleringhof, Adolfo del Campo, Apollonas S. Matsoukas-Roubeas
abstract: Krylov subspace methods provide an efficient tool for modeling any quantum initial value problem as a one dimensional chain. A time ordered path formulation, in which the dynamical generator successively splits probability between paths, yields a speed limit within such dynamical subspaces. For power law growing Lanczos coefficients $b_n \sim n^δ$ we find super ballistic lightcones, with an exponentially spreading lightcone for maximal growth $δ= 1$. Causality in the Krylov chain constrains the Lanczos coefficients to grow at most linearly. We illustrate the validity of the above in the $SL(2, R)$ and Heisenberg Weyl algebras, and in a many body skew field Ising model. Moreover, we extend the above bound to the family of $Q$ complexities. Lastly, mapping to a spin chain gives a Lieb Robinson bound analogue and opens the problem to standard condensed matter methods.
summary: This work establishes fundamental speed limits for how information can spread in quantum systems by mapping the dynamics onto a Krylov subspace chain. It derives bounds analogous to the Lieb-Robinson bound, showing that causality strictly limits the growth of system coefficients. The results are highly relevant for understanding the time scales of quantum evolution in many-body physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates fundamental speed limits and bounds on information propagation within the dynamical subspaces (Krylov subspaces) of isolated many-body quantum systems.
main_result: Causality constraints on the Lanczos coefficients imply that the information spread is bounded by a linear growth rate, leading to a Lieb-Robinson bound analogue for the Krylov chain.
method: The analysis uses Krylov subspace methods to model quantum dynamics as a 1D chain, deriving time-evolution amplitudes and comparing various theoretical bounds (Speed Limit, Corrected SL, Loschmidt Echo) against numerical results.
model_or_system: The study applies to general quantum initial value problems, specifically analyzing the dynamics of the $	ext{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, Heisenberg-Weyl algebra, and the Skew-Field Ising Model, which are mapped onto a spin chain Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Probability amplitudes $\varphi_n(t)$, Krylov complexity $K(t)$, and various time scales ($	au_{SL}^n$, $	au_{cSL}^n$, $	au_E$).
important_parameters: Lanczos coefficients $\{b_n\}$, the subspace dimension $D_K$, and the growth exponent $\delta$ for power-law coefficients.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the tridiagonalization of the dynamical generator into the Krylov basis and uses approximations for higher-order path expansions.
figures_summary: Figures compare different theoretical bounds (Speed Limit, Corrected SL, Loschmidt Echo) against the true numerical time for various models, and illustrate the relationship between Lanczos coefficients and causality bounds.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the general framework of information propagation in Krylov subspaces, deriving the speed limit based on causality, applying this to specific models ($	ext{SL}(2, \mathbb{R})$, SFIM), and finally comparing the accuracy of different bounding techniques.
why_interesting: The connection between information propagation bounds (like Lieb-Robinson bounds) and the structure of the Krylov subspace provides a powerful, general tool for analyzing dynamics in complex quantum systems, relevant to understanding thermalization and entanglement spreading.
